aaa_enabled.summary: Define a RADIUS or TACACS+ server and point an administrator account at it.
aaa_enabled.notes: FortiOS needs both halves: a server under 'config user', and an account with 'set remote-auth enable'. Either alone leaves administrative logins local.

secure_vty_transport.summary: Rewrite allowaccess on every interface, naming only the protocols that interface must serve.
secure_vty_transport.notes: 'set allowaccess' replaces the whole list; there is no incremental form. Restate every protocol the interface should keep.

vty_idle_timeout.summary: Set the administrative idle timeout to 10 minutes.
vty_idle_timeout.notes: 'admintimeout' is expressed in minutes on the device; the baseline stores it in seconds.

enable_secret_encrypted.summary: Set the password through the CLI so FortiOS stores and writes back only the hash.
cli: # FortiOS writes the credential back as: set password ENC <hash>
enable_secret_encrypted.notes: The 'ENC' keyword in front of a stored password is what marks it hashed. A 'set password' statement without it is a cleartext credential.

no_default_snmp_community.summary: Delete the default community and replace it with a non-default name limited to the management network.

http_server_disabled.summary: Remove http from allowaccess and redirect administrative GUI traffic to HTTPS.

ssh_version_2.summary: Disable SSHv1 compatibility explicitly, so the configuration states the enforced version.
ssh_version_2.notes: 'admin-ssh-v1' exists in FortiOS 6.x and was removed in 7.x, which speaks v2 only. A configuration that states neither leaves the enforced version to a release default, which is reported as NEEDS_REVIEW rather than guessed.

logging_enabled.summary: Enable a remote syslog server, and keep an on-box store as well.
logging_enabled.notes: Each log destination carries its own 'set status'. A server configured with 'set status disable' ships nothing and does not satisfy this control.

management_acl.summary: Give each administrator account a trusthost covering the management network only.
management_acl.notes: The factory trusthost is '0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0', which permits every source. An account is treated as restricted once at least one trusthost is narrower than that.

login_banner.summary: Turn on the pre-login banner and edit its text in the replacement message group.
login_banner.notes: Both banners default to 'disable', so a configuration that mentions neither shows no banner.

password_min_length.summary: Enable the password policy and set a minimum length.
password_min_length.notes: 'set status enable' is what puts the policy in force. A password-policy block with 'set status disable' enforces nothing however long its minimum-length says.

ntp_configured.summary: Point the device at your own NTP servers rather than the FortiGuard default.
ntp_configured.notes: A device left on 'set type fortiguard' is synchronised, but the configuration names no address, so this control reports NEEDS_REVIEW rather than passing or failing.

no_write_snmp_community.summary: Keep v1/v2c to queries and traps, and move any account that needs more to SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy.
no_write_snmp_community.notes: The FortiOS SNMP agent serves v1/v2c queries and sends traps, and offers no community-scoped write, so a FortiOS community is read-only by construction rather than by configuration. The control is still evaluated so that a FortiOS report answers the same question as the Cisco and Junos reports.
